Every narration clip in every chapter — Trial 1 and everything after it — is generated at exactly these values. Changing any one of them invalidates every existing clip and requires regenerating all of them in a single session, plus a minor version bump on the video system.
voice.voice_kind: pvc (professional voice clone) — from the sample filename

_settings_provenance.source: the sample filename ElevenLabs_2026-09-14T21_35_46_Amy_-_Natural_and_Sweet_pvc_sp72_s60_sb75_se0_b_m2.mp3, cross-checked against the settings screenshot
_settings_provenance.sp72_s60_sb75_se0: speed 0.72 · stability 0.60 · similarity_boost 0.75 · style 0.0 — each written as a percentage in the filename
_settings_provenance.screenshot_agrees: Speed near the left of its 0.7-1.2 track, Stability just past the middle, Similarity high, Style Exaggeration at None
_settings_provenance.use_speaker_boost: USER-APPROVED PRODUCTION SETTING. Michelle approved speaker boost ON for all Trial 1 narration on 2026-09-14: 'Speaker boost is explicitly approved on for all Trial 1 narration. Treat this as the production setting, not an inference from the reference filename.' It is no longer inferred from the `_b_` token in the reference sample's filename; that token is now corroboration, not the basis. The VALUE is unchanged (true), so the lock fingerprint is unchanged.

reference_sample.verified: Probed with ffprobe rather than taken on trust — every stated value matches.
reference_sample.status: APPROVED on 2026-09-14 and preserved as the voice reference for the OI Modular Video Production System. Any future question about whether a clip matches the approved voice is answered against this file.
reference_sample.not: This is NOT Trial 1 narration. It is a terminology and delivery test, and it is never cut into the video.
reference_sample.previous_filename: VALIDATION_SAMPLE_pending_approval.mp3 — renamed once Michelle designated it the voice-reference sample. Same file; sha256 verified identical across the rename.

preferred.why: The approved narration-master format, chosen 2026-09-15 as an explicit production decision after the first paid run returned HTTP 403: "output_format_not_allowed: Output format 'pcm_44100' is only available on the Pro tier and above." mp3_44100_128 is available on the current subscription. Masters are kept as the MP3 the API returns — they are NOT transcoded to WAV, which would add a decode/encode round trip without recovering anything the encoder already discarded.
preferred.honest_description: Lossy. One encode at generation, then one AAC encode at assembly. Do not describe these masters as lossless.

superseded.why_abandoned: Returned HTTP 403 output_format_not_allowed on the first paid run (scene S010). pcm_44100 requires the ElevenLabs Pro tier. Zero clips were generated and fail-fast stopped the other 23 requests, so nothing was charged for an unusable format.

output_format.note: Output format is a DELIVERY choice and sits OUTSIDE the voice lock. The lock covers voice_id, model_id and the five settings only. Changing the container changes nothing about the voice, and the lock fingerprint is unchanged.

loudness.rule: Normalise at final assembly, never by changing voice settings.
loudness.why: Stability, similarity and style shape the performance. Turning them to chase volume changes how the voice sounds and desynchronises the cut from the approved sample. Loudness is fixed once, on the finished mix.
loudness.how: ffmpeg loudnorm at assembly, applied to the assembled narration bed.

speaking_rate.measured_from: 159 words of VALIDATION_SCRIPT.txt read in 69.799s at speed 0.72
speaking_rate.effect: The old figure ran 5.1% fast. Every scene estimate is now derived from this measurement.
speaking_rate.note: Re-measure if the voice, model or speed setting changes. Speed 0.72 is well below the 1.0 default and is a large part of why.

generation_rules: Generate the validation sample first and get it approved. Nothing else until then.
Use the exact same voice, model and settings for every scene clip. No per-scene adjustment, for any reason.
Generate every clip in one session with identical settings. Clips generated weeks apart drift in tone and the cut hears it.
One clip per scene. Never one long read sliced afterwards — that is what makes a one-line correction expensive.
Never speed the voice up to fit a picture. The picture is cut to the speech.
Never change settings to make a clip louder. Normalise at assembly.
Model, settings and format are written into elevenlabs/generation_manifest.json on every `scripts` run, so any clip can be reproduced exactly.
voice._voice_id_provenance: Supplied by Michelle on 2026-09-14 alongside the voice name, model and the four settings, all of which match what was already recorded from the sample filename and screenshot. Not derived, not guessed.

lock.locked_by: Michelle — 'The validation sample is approved. Lock this voice ID and these settings for the OI modular video system.'
lock.scope: The whole OI Modular Video Production System, not Trial 1 alone.
change_procedure: A change to any locked value is a system-level change, not a scene edit.
Every clip already generated becomes invalid — tone drifts audibly between settings, and a half-regenerated cut is worse than either.
Re-measure words-per-second from a new validation sample; every scene duration estimate is derived from it.
Regenerate all clips in one session, then rebuild every scene.

voice._outstanding_note: Nothing outstanding. Speaker boost was the last inferred value and is now a user-approved production setting.
